_comment: Declared blind spots of the quality defence, as measured by scripts/quality_matrix.py.
This file is a registry, not a to-do list: tests/test_quality_matrix.py fails when the
measured set of holes differs from the set declared here, in EITHER direction. A new
blind spot therefore cannot land silently - it has to be written down with an exit
criterion first - and a hole that gets closed cannot stay here as decoration, because
an obsolete entry reads as an open one.
Fields: id = '<kind>:<name>' exactly as measured; opened = date the measurement found
it; exit = the concrete, checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must list every id in this file and no others.
An empty list is a measured state, not an aspiration: the same gate that fails on an
unregistered hole fails on a registered one the measurement no longer reproduces.

holes.why: The instruction-count gate is the only reproducible perf instrument in the set (two runner images agree to 0.0018%), and `ir_gate` compiles against pyrs-yaml-core, pyrs-ast, pyrs-schema, pyrs-json and pyrs-toml - never pyrs-yaml, the crate that serves the Python API. So the conversion every user goes through (`safe_load`, `to_python`) has no number that can gate a regression: wall-time CodSpeed covers it, and this repository's own notes report that channel swinging +-7.7/-10.5/-9.8% on runs that did strictly less work. Found by deriving the harness's build graph, not by reading scenario names.
holes.exit: A scenario in an `ir_gate` bench target compiled against the binding crate (PyO3 + a Python interpreter, so `PYO3_PYTHON` and the `abi3` feature are in scope) measures the AST-to-Python conversion in counted instructions, with its own number committed through `python scripts/ir_gate.py --update --only <name>`; the probe then stops emitting this hole because the crate is in the graph.
